_meta._comment: Source of truth for AgentRelay's user-facing strings. Every other <lang>.json is measured against this file by check.mjs. Do NOT translate _meta. INTERPOLATION: variables are written {name} with single braces; a literal brace is not used anywhere in this catalogue. A translation MUST use exactly the same set of {name} placeholders as en.json for the same key — same names, no extras, none dropped (check.mjs fails otherwise). The reason is blunt: a format string that references {sha} in code but is missing from a translation is a runtime crash, not a cosmetic bug. PLURALS: a value that is an object whose keys are CLDR plural categories (zero/one/two/few/many/other) is a plural message; the count that selects the form is the variable named {count}. English has two forms (one/other). Hebrew has four (one/two/many/other), Arabic six, Russian four — each language file MUST supply exactly the categories its language requires. BIDI: right-to-left files (he, ar) wrap every left-to-right run — file paths, git SHAs, shell commands, URLs, $amounts, config paths, ntfy topics, timestamps — in an isolate U+2066…U+2069 so it does not visually shatter the surrounding sentence. See README section 'Bidi'.

cli.about._comment: clap --help one-liner for the whole binary. 'locally' is the product's core promise: the daemon runs on your machine.
cli.about.value: Supervise overnight AI coding-agent runs — locally.

error.prefix._comment: Prepended to any fatal CLI error, e.g. 'agentrelay: no .agentrelay here'. The program name is literal and NOT translated.

error.no_workspace._comment: Daemon opened in a directory that was never initialised. {dir} is the literal folder name '.agentrelay' (keep it as-is). The backticked command is literal.

error.bad_config._comment: The config file exists but is not valid JSON. {path} is a file path (LTR), {err} is the parser's message (English, LTR). The refusal is deliberate: running with guards silently disabled is the failure mode this whole product exists to prevent.
error.bad_config.value:
{path} is not valid config: {err}
Fix it (or delete it to use defaults) — refusing to run with guards silently disabled.

error.budget_reached._comment: A turn was refused because the spending cap would be crossed. {reason} is one of the cost.stop.* strings.
error.budget_reached.value: budget reached — not starting a turn: {reason}

error.no_baseline._comment: complete_unit refused to checkpoint because the tree was already dirty and no `agentrelay begin` snapshot exists, so the supervisor cannot separate the human's work from the agent's. {count} is a file count (plural). Backticked commands are literal.

value.one: not checkpointed: {count} file was already uncommitted and no baseline was recorded, so the supervisor cannot tell your work from the agent's. Run `agentrelay begin` before the agent starts, or commit/stash your own changes first. Nothing was touched.
value.other: not checkpointed: {count} files were already uncommitted and no baseline was recorded, so the supervisor cannot tell your work from the agent's. Run `agentrelay begin` before the agent starts, or commit/stash your own changes first. Nothing was touched.

init.done._comment: Printed by `agentrelay init`. '.agentrelay/', 'config.json', 'agentrelay.db' are literal file names — keep them.

init.next._comment: Follow-up hint after init. The backticked command and the file path are literal.
init.next.value: Next: `agentrelay run "<your task>"` — or edit .agentrelay/config.json first.

status.db._comment: Status field label. {path} is the database file path (LTR). Keep the label short; it is column-aligned in the terminal.

status.schema._comment: Status field: database schema version. {version} is an integer; the leading 'v' is literal.

status.missions._comment: Status field: how many missions exist. {count} is an integer.

status.engine._comment: Status field: which agent binary is configured (e.g. 'claude'). {program} is a program name (LTR).

status.keep_awake._comment: Status field: whether the machine is kept from sleeping. {value} is true/false.

status.state._comment: Status field: mission state plus its plain-language meaning. {state} is a state id like 'running' (LTR), {meaning} is one of state.describe.*.

status.waiting_marker._comment: Extra line under status.state, shown only when the mission needs a human. The caret points up at the state line.
status.waiting_marker.value: ^ nothing will happen until you act.

status.spent._comment: Last line of status: how much has been spent. {budget} is a cost.describe.* sentence; {spent} is a dollar amount formatted to 2 decimals (LTR).

run.finished._comment: Header after `agentrelay run` completes one turn.

run.events._comment: How many stream events were seen this turn. {count} integer.

run.tokens._comment: Token usage for the turn. {count} integer.

run.completed._comment: Whether the agent signalled completion. {value} true/false.

run.interrupted._comment: Shown when a guard stopped the turn; followed by one run.violation line per guard.

run.violation._comment: One blocked action. {reason} is a guard reason code (LTR, e.g. 'guard.no_push'); {detail} is the offending command (LTR).

run.rate_limited._comment: The turn hit the provider quota and will resume. {at} is an RFC3339 timestamp (LTR), {ms} an integer of milliseconds.

doctor.title._comment: Header of `agentrelay doctor`, which checks required tools are installed.

doctor.ok._comment: A tool was found. {tool} is its name (LTR), {path} its location (LTR). '[OK]' is a literal status marker.

doctor.missing._comment: A tool was not found. {tool} name (LTR), {hint} is one of which.hint.* explaining how to install it. '[--]' is a literal marker.

doctor.no_claude._comment: Shown when the agent binary 'claude' is absent. Explains that the safety machinery still works but there is nothing to supervise. 'claude', 'guards', 'checkpoints' — 'claude' is a literal program name.
doctor.no_claude.value:
Without `claude` the daemon can supervise nothing — everything else
here (guards, checkpoints, the report) still works, but there is no agent.

doctor.missing_required._comment: Fatal error when git or node is missing (claude is optional; git/node are not).

validate.none._comment: No validators are configured. The parenthetical points at the exact config field. The path and 'validators' are literal.

validate.result._comment: One validator's outcome. {status} is the literal token PASS or FAIL (see validate.pass/validate.fail), {name} the validator name (LTR), {ms} its duration in ms.

validate.pass._comment: The literal token substituted into {status} when a check passed. Kept short and uppercase; it is column-aligned against FAIL.

validate.fail._comment: The literal token substituted into {status} when a check failed. Must stay the same width family as PASS for alignment and must read as clearly negative.

validate.all_passed._comment: Every configured validator passed. The parenthetical is the product's core claim: this is evidence from a command, not the model's self-report.
validate.all_passed.value: All validators passed — unit complete (evidence, not the model's word).

validate.failed._comment: Fatal error string when validators failed. 'NOT' is emphatic on purpose.
validate.failed.value: validators failed — unit is NOT complete

hook.deny.unreadable._comment: A PreToolUse hook could not parse the tool call, so it refuses. {err} is the parser message (LTR). Fail-closed by design: refusing what we cannot read is the whole point of a guard.
hook.deny.unreadable.value: AgentRelay could not read this tool call ({err}), so it is refused rather than guessed at.

hook.deny.no_tool_name._comment: The tool call had an empty tool name; refused.
hook.deny.no_tool_name.value: AgentRelay received a tool call with no tool name — refused.

hook.deny.blocked._comment: A guard blocked a tool call. {reasons} is a '; '-joined list of reason codes with details (LTR). The second sentence is addressed to the AGENT and must survive translation: it tells the model not to route around the guard, which matters as much as the refusal itself.
hook.deny.blocked.value: Blocked by AgentRelay: {reasons}. This is a guard the user configured for this run — do not retry it, and do not work around it. Choose a different approach or stop and report.

hook.deny.no_guards._comment: The hook could not load the workspace config, so it refuses rather than run unguarded. {err} parser/IO message (LTR).
hook.deny.no_guards.value: AgentRelay could not load its guards ({err}), so this tool call is refused rather than run unguarded.

install_hook.already._comment: `agentrelay install-hook` found our hook already present or the settings file too malformed to edit safely. {path} is the settings.json path (LTR).
install_hook.already.value: Already installed, or {path} is not in a shape we can safely edit — nothing was changed.

install_hook.installed_detail._comment: Explains what changed after install: guards now block pre-execution rather than reacting, and the user's other hooks were preserved.
install_hook.installed_detail.value:
Guards now BLOCK a forbidden tool call before it runs, instead of
stopping the agent after the fact. Your other hooks were left alone.

fits.go._comment: `agentrelay fits` says a unit of the requested length fits in the remaining quota window. {minutes} integer.
fits.go.value: Go — a ~{minutes} minute unit fits in what is left of the window.

fits.go_blind._comment: No quota window is known yet, so we allow the unit but say we are guessing.
fits.go_blind.value:
Go, but blind: no quota window has been reported yet, so there is
nothing to reason about. Run a turn and the provider will tell us.

fits.wait._comment: The unit would be cut off by the quota reset, so wait. {minutes} integer of the requested unit length.
fits.wait.value: Wait — a ~{minutes} minute unit would be cut off by the quota window.

fits.wait_reopens._comment: Sub-line of fits.wait: when the window reopens. {at} RFC3339 timestamp (LTR).

fits.wait_minutes._comment: Sub-line of fits.wait: how long to wait. {count} is a minute count (plural).

fits.wait_why._comment: Explains why waiting beats starting: a unit stopped mid-run is half-done, unverified and has no restore point.
fits.wait_why.value:
Being stopped mid-unit costs more than waiting: the work would be
half-done, unvalidated and uncheckpointed.

begin.clean._comment: `agentrelay begin` on a clean tree: nothing pre-existing to protect.
begin.clean.value: Tree is clean. Everything the agent changes from here is its own.

begin.dirty_intro._comment: The tree already had uncommitted files; they are recorded so a later checkpoint will not sweep them into the agent's commit. {count} file count (plural).

value.one: {count} file is already uncommitted and will be left alone:
value.other: {count} files are already uncommitted and will be left alone:

begin.and_more._comment: Truncation line after listing the first few files. {count} is how many more are hidden (plural). The leading character is an ellipsis.

begin.dirty_note._comment: Reassures that those pre-existing files stay out of this unit's checkpoints. {unit} is the unit id (LTR).
begin.dirty_note.value: They will NOT be committed by any checkpoint for unit `{unit}`.

done.none._comment: `agentrelay done` with no validators configured: refuses to certify. Path and 'validators' literal.

done.none_detail._comment: Second line: nothing was checkpointed because there is no evidence to certify completion.
done.none_detail.value: Nothing was checkpointed: without evidence there is nothing to certify.

done.no_evidence._comment: Fatal error: a unit cannot be complete with no completion evidence.
done.no_evidence.value: no completion evidence — unit is NOT complete

done.not_checkpointed._comment: Validators failed, so the work stays uncommitted in the tree for the human to inspect.
done.not_checkpointed.value: Not checkpointed — your work is still in the working tree, uncommitted.

done.failed._comment: Fatal error when the completion gate failed.
done.failed.value: validators failed — unit is NOT complete

done.checkpointed._comment: A checkpoint commit was made. {sha} is a 7-char git SHA (LTR), {count} the number of files (plural), {branch} the branch name or 'detached HEAD' (LTR).

done.detached_head._comment: Substituted into {branch} above when HEAD is detached. Kept as the literal git term.

done.left_alone._comment: Sub-line: files the human had already changed were deliberately not committed. {count} file count (plural), {paths} a comma-joined list of paths (LTR).

value.one: Left alone ({count} file you had already changed): {paths}
value.other: Left alone ({count} files you had already changed): {paths}

done.undo._comment: How to undo just this unit. {cmd} is a full git command (LTR) — in RTL files it MUST be isolated so it does not reorder against the label.

done.rewind._comment: How to rewind to this checkpoint later. {cmd} full git command (LTR); isolate in RTL files.

done.nothing_to_commit._comment: Validators passed but the tree was already clean, so there was nothing to checkpoint.
done.nothing_to_commit.value: Validators passed; nothing to checkpoint (the tree was already clean).

done.checkpoint_error._comment: Validators passed but the checkpoint commit itself failed. {err} git error (LTR).
done.checkpoint_error.value: Validators passed, but the checkpoint could not be made: {err}

report.provenance.verified._comment: SEVERITY WORD — do not weaken. Marks a line proven by a command's exit code: hard evidence. Must stay clearly distinct from RECORDED (merely observed) and ESTIMATED (a guess). Rendered inside brackets: [VERIFIED]. In many languages 'verified' and 'recorded' collapse to one word — pick two genuinely different words and note it in the README if you must strain.

report.provenance.recorded._comment: SEVERITY WORD — do not weaken. Marks a line the supervisor observed directly (a commit exists, a guard fired). Weaker than VERIFIED, stronger than ESTIMATED. Must stay distinct from both.

report.provenance.estimated._comment: SEVERITY WORD — do not weaken. Marks a number computed from a rule of thumb, never a measurement. Must read as clearly less trustworthy than VERIFIED and RECORDED.

report.header._comment: First line of the morning report. {mission} is the mission id (LTR).

report.nothing._comment: Whole body when literally nothing ran. Said plainly rather than dressed up as a quiet success. Backticked command literal.
report.nothing.value:
Nothing ran. No units were completed, no checkpoints were made, and no
validators reported. If you expected work overnight, something stopped
before it started — check `agentrelay status`.

report.line._comment: One report line. {tag} is a translated provenance word, {text} the line body. The brackets frame the tag.

report.footer._comment: Explains the tags at the bottom of every non-empty report. The three provenance words here MUST match report.provenance.* exactly. This is the key that makes the tags mean something instead of being decoration.
report.footer.value:
Every line above is labelled by where it came from. VERIFIED means a
command ran and its exit code decided it. ESTIMATED is a rule of thumb.
Nothing the agent merely claimed appears here at all.

report.headline.nothing._comment: One-line phone headline when nothing ran.

report.headline.failed._comment: Phone headline when units failed. {count} = units done (plural selector), {failed} = number that FAILED. 'FAILED' is emphatic.

value.one: AgentRelay: {count} unit done, {failed} FAILED — work left uncommitted for you
value.other: AgentRelay: {count} units done, {failed} FAILED — work left uncommitted for you

report.headline.unverified._comment: Phone headline when some units had no validators. {count} = units done (plural selector), {unverified} = number NOT VERIFIED.

value.one: AgentRelay: {count} unit done, {unverified} NOT VERIFIED — no validators ran
value.other: AgentRelay: {count} units done, {unverified} NOT VERIFIED — no validators ran

report.headline.uncheckpointed._comment: Phone headline when passing units produced no restore point. {count} = units passed (plural selector), {uncheckpointed} = number with no checkpoint.

value.one: AgentRelay: {count} unit passed but {uncheckpointed} has NO restore point
value.other: AgentRelay: {count} units passed but {uncheckpointed} has NO restore point

report.headline.ok._comment: Phone headline for a clean night. {count} = units done (plural).

value.one: AgentRelay: {count} unit done, all validators passed
value.other: AgentRelay: {count} units done, all validators passed

report.line.unverified._comment: Report body line for a unit nobody checked. {unit} unit id (LTR). Path and 'validators' literal. 'NOT VERIFIED' is emphatic.
report.line.unverified.value: {unit}: NOT VERIFIED — no validators ran, so nothing about this unit is known. Add validators to .agentrelay/config.json

report.line.checks_passed._comment: Report body line for a passing unit. {unit} unit id (LTR), {count} number of checks (plural), {names} comma-joined validator names (LTR).

report.line.uncheckpointed._comment: Report body line: unit passed but has no commit to return to. {unit} unit id (LTR), {worktree} an optional ' (worktree: /path)' fragment or empty — see report.line.worktree_suffix.
report.line.uncheckpointed.value: {unit}: passed but WAS NOT CHECKPOINTED — there is no commit to go back to{worktree}

report.line.worktree_suffix._comment: Optional tail appended to report.line.uncheckpointed naming the worktree. {path} is a directory path (LTR). Note the leading space.

report.line.failed._comment: Report body line for a failed unit. {unit} unit id (LTR), {names} the checks that did not pass (LTR). Tells the human the work is uncommitted and where it is.
report.line.failed.value: {unit}: FAILED — {names} did not pass. This work was NOT committed; it is still in your working tree

report.line.checkpoint._comment: Report body line naming a checkpoint and how to read it. {sha} 7-char git SHA (LTR), {id} unit id (LTR). The backticked `git show {sha}` is a command (LTR). RTL files MUST isolate all three so the sentence does not reorder.

report.line.tool_denied._comment: The agent itself confirmed a tool call was refused and never ran (VERIFIED-grade). {tool} tool name (LTR).
report.line.tool_denied.value: the agent reported that its {tool} call was refused and never ran

report.line.fixloop_gaveup._comment: The fix loop stopped and left the problem for the human. {reason} is a fixloop.giveup.* string.
report.line.fixloop_gaveup.value: the fix loop stopped and left this for you — {reason}

report.line.drift._comment: Possible drift from the task (ESTIMATED-grade — a heuristic). {summary} is a short drift description (may contain paths, LTR).

report.line.blocked._comment: A guard fired. {guard} guard name (LTR), {reason} what the agent tried, {sep} either ' — ' or empty, {detail} the offending command (LTR). RTL: isolate {guard} and {detail}.
report.line.blocked.value: BLOCKED by {guard}: the agent tried {reason}{sep}{detail}. The turn was stopped.

report.line.dirty_files._comment: Files left uncommitted in the tree. {count} file count (plural), {paths} comma-joined paths, first five (LTR).

value.one: {count} file left uncommitted in the working tree: {paths}
value.other: {count} files left uncommitted in the working tree: {paths}

report.line.saved._comment: ESTIMATED-grade line about content not re-sent because files were unchanged. {kb} kilobytes (integer), {tokens} approx tokens (integer). The '~' and 'rough' both signal this is an estimate, not a measurement — keep that hedge.
report.line.saved.value: ~{kb} KB of file content was not re-sent because the files were unchanged (~{tokens} tokens, at a rough 4 bytes per token)

report.notify.pushed._comment: Confirmation that the headline was pushed to the configured notifier.

report.notify.off._comment: The user passed --notify but notifications are disabled. Path and 'notify' literal.
report.notify.off.value: (--notify given, but notifications are off — set `notify` in .agentrelay/config.json; nothing was sent)

report.notify.failed._comment: Delivery failed but the report still stands; the night's outcome does not depend on a phone server. {err} the delivery error (LTR).
report.notify.failed.value: notification failed (the report above still stands): {err}

fix.green_after._comment: Fixed after some attempts. {count} number of attempts (plural).

fix.stopped_after._comment: Gave up after some attempts. {count} number of attempts (plural).

fix.reason._comment: Indented reason line under fix.stopped_after. {why} is a fixloop.giveup.* string.

fix.waiting._comment: Explains the mission is now parked for a human. 'waiting_input' is a literal state id — keep it.
fix.waiting.value: The mission is now `waiting_input`: it will not continue by itself.

fix.still_failing._comment: Fatal error when fix gave up.
fix.still_failing.value: the checks are still failing — a person is needed

checkpoints.none._comment: No checkpoints exist yet. The backticked command is literal.
checkpoints.none.value: No checkpoints yet — run `agentrelay done "<what the unit did>"`.

checkpoints.hint._comment: How to see what changed after a checkpoint. The git command is literal (LTR).
checkpoints.hint.value: To see what came after one:  git diff --stat <sha> HEAD

serve.listening._comment: The IPC server started. {addr} is host:port (LTR). 'http://' literal.

serve.token._comment: Where the loopback auth token was written and which endpoints exist. Path and endpoint names literal (LTR).
serve.token.value: token written to .agentrelay/ipc.json — GET /status, POST /run, GET /health

state.describe.draft._comment: Plain-language meaning of mission state 'draft' for `status`.

state.describe.waiting_input._comment: Meaning of 'waiting_input'. The emphasis matters: this state never self-resumes, and telling the user so prevents them waiting forever.
state.describe.waiting_input.value: STOPPED, waiting for you — it will not continue by itself

state.describe.rate_limited._comment: Meaning of 'rate_limited'. This one DOES resume on its own.
state.describe.rate_limited.value: out of quota; will resume when the window reopens

state.describe.paused.value: paused by you; resume when ready

state.describe.stopping._comment: Meaning of 'stopping' — in progress, needs nobody.
state.describe.stopping.value: stopping — killing processes and writing the final state

state.illegal._comment: An illegal state transition was refused. {from} and {to} are state ids (LTR), {why} one of state.why.*.

state.why.terminal._comment: Why a finished mission cannot move: it is final. {from} is a state id (LTR). The advice to start a new mission is load-bearing.
state.why.terminal.value: {from} is final. A mission that has finished must not restart on its own — start a new mission instead

state.why.stopping._comment: Why a stop-in-progress can only finish.
state.why.stopping.value: a stop in progress can only finish, not turn into something else

state.why.draft.value: a mission cannot go back to being unstarted

state.why.stopped._comment: Why 'stopped' is only reached through 'stopping' (so processes are actually killed first). 'stopped' and 'stopping' are literal state ids.
state.why.stopped.value: reach `stopped` through `stopping`, so processes are actually killed first

cost.describe.none._comment: Shown in `status` when no spending cap is set. Saying it out loud matters: a cap you believe is set but is not is worse than none.
cost.describe.none.value: No spending cap is set. AgentRelay will not stop the run on cost.

cost.describe.mission._comment: A per-mission cap is set. {mission} dollar amount, 2 decimals (LTR).

cost.describe.turn._comment: A per-turn cap is set. {turn} dollar amount (LTR).

cost.describe.both._comment: Both caps set. {mission} and {turn} dollar amounts (LTR).
cost.describe.both.value: Spending cap: ${mission} for this mission, ${turn} per turn.

cost.stop.turn_cap._comment: A turn was stopped for exceeding the per-turn cap. {worst} projected turn cost, {cap} the per-turn cap (both dollar amounts, LTR).
cost.stop.turn_cap.value: the next turn could cost about ${worst}, over the ${cap} per-turn cap

cost.stop.mission_over._comment: Already at or over the mission cap. {spent} spent so far, {cap} the mission cap (dollars, LTR).
cost.stop.mission_over.value: ${spent} spent, at or over the ${cap} cap for this mission

cost.stop.mission_would_pass._comment: Starting the next turn would cross the mission cap. {spent}, {worst}, {cap} dollar amounts (LTR).
cost.stop.mission_would_pass.value: ${spent} spent and the next turn could add about ${worst}, which would pass the ${cap} cap

isolation.off._comment: Isolation is disabled: the agent runs directly on the host. Stated bluntly because a user who believes isolation is on when it is off is the worst case.
isolation.off.value: Isolation is OFF. The agent runs directly on this machine, with your network and your files.

isolation.on._comment: Isolation is on. {image} is the container image name (LTR).
isolation.on.value: Isolation is ON: the agent runs inside `{image}`, with only the workspace mounted.

isolation.net_off._comment: Network fully off inside the container — the flag that makes exfiltration impossible rather than merely unlikely. Appended after isolation.on.
isolation.net_off.value: Network: OFF. Nothing the agent runs can reach the internet.

isolation.net_on._comment: Network partly allowed. {hosts} comma-joined host list (LTR). The NOTE is a real security caveat — Docker cannot enforce a host allowlist alone — and must not be softened.
isolation.net_on.value: Network: ON, limited to {hosts}. NOTE: Docker cannot enforce a host allowlist by itself — this needs a proxy in front, so treat it as network ON until you have one.

isolation.blocker._comment: Isolation was requested but Docker is unusable, so the run refuses rather than silently dropping isolation. 'isolation.image' and 'Docker' are literal.
isolation.blocker.value: isolation is configured but Docker is not available (not installed, or the daemon is not running). Start Docker, or remove `isolation.image` to run without it — AgentRelay will not silently run unisolated when you asked for isolation.

notify.off._comment: Notifications disabled — the default. This is the only network path in the daemon, so silence is the default and must be visible.
notify.off.value: Notifications are OFF. Nothing leaves this machine.

notify.on._comment: Notifications enabled: states exactly what leaves the machine. {server} the ntfy server URL (LTR), {topic} the topic name (LTR). The embedded example "2 unit(s) done, 1 FAILED" is illustrative literal text; keep it recognisable. The promise that no file contents/diffs/paths are sent is a privacy guarantee — do not drop it.
notify.on.value:
Notifications are ON. A short line — a title and a headline such as "2 unit(s) done, 1 FAILED" — will be sent to {server} on topic "{topic}".
No file contents, diffs, prompts, command output or paths are ever sent.

notify.public_warning._comment: Appended when the server is the public ntfy.sh: anyone who guesses the topic can read the notifications. 'ntfy.sh' and 'server' are literal.
notify.public_warning.value: NOTE: ntfy.sh is a public server run by someone else, and anyone who guesses your topic name can read your notifications. Use a long random topic, or self-host and set `server` to your own instance.

notify.title._comment: The notification title/app name. Product name — NOT translated in any language.

drift.summary.unchecked._comment: No scope was declared, so drift could not be checked. This must NOT read the same as 'we checked and it was clean' — the distinction is the point.
drift.summary.unchecked.value: Drift was not checked: this unit did not say what it would touch.

drift.summary.clean._comment: Scope was declared and the work stayed inside it.
drift.summary.clean.value: The changes stayed inside what this unit said it would touch.

drift.summary.header._comment: Header before the list of drift signals. {count} number of signals (plural).

value.one: {count} sign that the work drifted from the task:
value.other: {count} signs that the work drifted from the task:

drift.summary.signal._comment: One drift signal, indented under the header. {text} a drift.signal.* string.

drift.summary.footer._comment: Reminds the reader this is a heuristic, not a verdict, and the work was not stopped. Both hedges are deliberate.
drift.summary.footer.value: This is a heuristic, not a verdict — the work was not stopped. Read the diff before trusting it.

drift.signal.out_of_scope._comment: A changed file outside the declared scope. {path} file path (LTR).
drift.signal.out_of_scope.value: {path} is outside everything this unit said it would touch

drift.signal.too_many_files._comment: More files changed than the unit expected. {count} number changed (plural selector), {expected} the declared maximum.

value.one: {count} file changed; the unit expected at most {expected}
value.other: {count} files changed; the unit expected at most {expected}

drift.signal.unrelated._comment: A changed file in an area that suggests different work. {path} file path (LTR), {why} one of drift.area.*.

drift.area.ci.value: changes how CI runs, which is not usually part of a code task

drift.area.dockerfile._comment: Why touching a Dockerfile is flagged.
drift.area.dockerfile.value: changes how the project is built or shipped

drift.area.env._comment: Why touching a .env file is flagged.
drift.area.env.value: touches configuration that usually holds secrets

fixloop.prompt.header._comment: Sent TO the agent to start a fix attempt. Instructional English aimed at the model. Followed by the failing validator output.
fixloop.prompt.header.value: The checks for this unit are failing. Fix ONLY what is needed to make them pass.

fixloop.prompt.section._comment: Header before one failing validator's output in the fix prompt. {name} validator name (LTR).

fixloop.prompt.footer._comment: The rules that stop a green build from being meaningless: don't edit tests, don't disable checks, don't widen scope; if you can't fix it honestly, say so. Addressed to the agent.
fixloop.prompt.footer.value: Do not change the tests to make them pass, do not disable a check, and do not widen the scope of this unit. If the failure cannot be fixed without doing one of those things, stop and say so instead — that answer is more useful than a green build that means nothing.

fixloop.giveup.no_validators._comment: The loop cannot fix toward nothing. Same rule as the completion gate: no evidence is not success.
fixloop.giveup.no_validators.value: no validators are configured, so there is nothing to fix towards

fixloop.giveup.stuck._comment: Two attempts failed identically, so the agent is stuck, not progressing. {attempt} the attempt number (integer).
fixloop.giveup.stuck.value: attempt {attempt} failed in exactly the same way as the one before it. The agent is stuck rather than making progress, and another try will cost quota without changing anything

fixloop.giveup.cap._comment: The hard attempt cap was reached. {max} the configured maximum (integer).
fixloop.giveup.cap.value: {max} fix attempts did not make the checks pass. Stopping so a person can look, rather than spending the rest of the night on it

which.hint.claude._comment: How to install the agent binary. The npm command is literal (LTR). The 'new terminal' step is the one Windows users miss.
which.hint.claude.value: not found on PATH — install with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, then open a new terminal so PATH is refreshed

which.hint.git.value: not found on PATH — install Git and reopen your terminal

which.hint.node._comment: How to get Node. '18' is a version number.
which.hint.node.value: not found on PATH — install Node.js 18 or newer

which.hint.other._comment: Generic not-found. {program} the missing program name (LTR).
